A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched, including v3's added Sections D.3–D.4.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, inference comparisons, robustness tests, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds class-level analyses of performance under differing fine-grained label availability.

M1.justification: Text-Attr, Taxon-SSL, their losses and architectural components, combined training strategies, and free-grained inference rules remain unchanged. The additions analyze existing methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet-F, iNat21-mini-F, CUB-F, CUB-Rand, Aircraft-Rand, and irregular WordNet hierarchy evaluations. Sections D.3–D.4 examine existing ImageNet-F classes without adding datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged. D.3 retains the Text-Attr (H-ViT) versus Taxon-SSL comparison, while D.4 breaks down the already reported ImageNet-F comparison between Text-Attr (H-CAST) and H-CAST.

E3.justification: D.4 adds an analysis protocol grouping classes into low-shot (<30), mid-shot (30–200), and many-shot (>200) fine-grained label regimes and examining per-class accuracy differences. Existing training budgets, data splits, model configurations, and benchmark metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: D.3 expands the existing Figure 6 label-availability analysis into separate frequency-bin panels. D.4 adds a diagnostic analysis of where text guidance improves H-CAST across classes. These extend an existing analytical question; previous ablations and robustness tests are retained.

E5.justification: D.2 retains the same three-seed averaging and reported variance range of 0.1–1.8. The added analyses introduce no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 13 reports per-class Text-Attr (H-CAST) gains over H-CAST, generally larger among low-/mid-shot classes but including negative gains. Existing scores remain unchanged, including ImageNet-F FPA of 57.59% for H-CAST and 63.20% for Text-Attr (H-CAST) in Figure 5b. Figure 12 subdivides existing Figure 6 results.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, and loss equations in Section 4 and Appendix H are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about free-grained recognition, benchmark construction, the two learning methods, and consistency-based inference. The additions provide supporting analysis without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: D.4 newly attributes larger gains over H-CAST in low-/mid-shot classes to complementary textual supervision and smaller many-shot gains to sufficient available supervision. D.3 mostly elaborates the existing method-preference interpretation. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, caption-generation instructions and cost, and the code/data access link are retained. Appendices F.5, G, and H provide the same reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix I are unchanged. Reference differences concern updated page back-references following the appendix additions.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix subsections D.3–D.4, corresponding contents entries, and brief cross-references in Sections 5.2–5.3. Remaining changes are local wording and text-flow adjustments, without substantial rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds the six-panel Figure 12 and classwise-gain Figure 13, and adds grid/frame styling to Figure 6 without changing its plotted values. Earlier Figures 12–13 become Figures 14–15; other changes are limited layout shifts.

improvement.justification: D.3's frequency-stratified panels and D.4's per-class H-CAST comparison modestly improve transparency about where text guidance helps, while retaining the methods and headline results. The added description of gains as consistent needs qualification because Figure 13 includes negative class-level differences, but the additional diagnostic evidence provides a limited net improvement.
